name: MIAFASCIA
address: 3753 NE 163rd St, North Miami Beach, FL 33160, United States
niche: massage therapist / myofascial release & recovery (fascia therapy)
website_check: Google Maps detail shows no website field ('Add website' shown, website=null). Checked miafascia.com, miafascia.net, miafascia.co, miafascia.us and miafascianorthmiamibeach.com via DNS: all NXDOMAIN (no domain registered). Web search for 'MIAFASCIA North Miami Beach instagram' and 'MIAFASCIA Ivan massage' found no personal domain, Instagram or Facebook page; only third-party directory mentions (Atly listing, Thumbtack mention of a therapist named Ivan with no confirmed link). No own site exists.

hours.source: Google Maps hours field (scraped 2026-11-23; Thu/Fri carried a holiday-week 'hours might differ' note for Thanksgiving/Black Friday which was generalized to the standard weekday hours for the site, not treated as a permanent change)

language_evidence: All 5 Google reviews pulled are written in English. No Spanish-language branding, flyer or caption found anywhere in the limited public presence (Atly/Thumbtack mentions, Google Maps). Business name 'MIAFASCIA' is a stylized portmanteau (Mia + Fascia), not a Spanish phrase. North Miami Beach is bilingual but no direct evidence points to Spanish as primary for this specific business, so English is used as the default language with full ES toggle per pipeline rule.
therapist_name: Ivan (named as the practitioner in every review found; no last name published anywhere public). A Google Maps gallery photo also shows the owner wearing a shirt with the MIAFASCIA logo at a 'Miami Massage Championship' community event, confirming he is the practitioner/owner.
services_real: Myofascial release (the business's own name; mentioned verbatim in 2 reviews as 'myofascial massage')
Deep tissue massage (mentioned in reviews for lower back and shoulder pain)
Cupping therapy (visible in 2 of the business's own Google photos: cupping marks on a client's back)
Red light therapy (mentioned in reviews; a large red light panel is visible in 2 of the business's own Google photos over the treatment table)
Electrical muscle stimulation / EMS (mentioned verbatim in 1 review alongside red light therapy and deep tissue)
Sports massage / recovery work for chronic pain and sports-related issues (mentioned in reviews)
Kinesio taping (visible in 1 of the business's own Google photos, KT-brand tape applied to a client's back)
pricing_note: No prices published anywhere found (Google Maps has no menu/pricing field, no booking platform page found). Site uses 'Call for pricing' per adapted-variant rule.

photos.source: Google Maps business photo gallery (9 photos cycled via gmaps_photocycle.js, 1 exact duplicate found, 8 unique real photos; all visually curated one by one, not chosen by filename)

used.desc: Treatment room bathed in red light therapy panel glow, massage table draped in grey, zen rug. Used as hero (most atmospheric, distinctive real photo, matches the crimson palette chosen for the site).
Close-up of the red light therapy panel and 'TheraTouch' EMS device control screen. Used in the Experience/About section to show real equipment.
Kinesio (KT) tape applied to a client's shoulder/back, cozy room corner visible (side table, candle). No face visible. Used as the wide gallery tile.
Close-up of cupping therapy cups on a client's lower back/hip. No face visible. Used as gallery tile.
Client standing after a cupping session, cupping marks visible on back, hands on hips, back of head only (no face). Used as gallery tile showing visible results.

Cropped headshot of Ivan (owner/therapist) from an outdoor photo at a 'Miami Massage Championship' community event, wearing a MIAFASCIA-branded shirt. Used ONLY as small avatar in nav/footer/experience per no-portraits-in-gallery rule, never as a gallery tile.

discarded: Exact duplicate of the hero photo (same red-light room shot returned twice by Google Maps)
A second close-up of the red light/EMS device from a different angle and worse crop than the one used (redundant)
A mirror selfie of Ivan in the treatment room (casual, not premium, owner selfie rule: never in gallery, and this one was not flattering enough even for the avatar)
A standing-back photo with a full cupping grid PLUS a dumbbell placed on the client's spine: visually confusing/odd for a premium gallery, discarded

brand_vibe: The real studio photos are dominated by deep red light therapy ambiance (a large red LED panel lit over the table, bathing the whole room red) plus black/orange kinesio tape and cupping marks. Site built on templates/dark-v2 (Pure Artistry skeleton) retinted from gold to a crimson/garnet 'recovery clinic' palette to match the actual photographed environment, a strong, distinctive match rather than a generic template look.
template_base: dark-v2 (Pure Artistry skeleton), anchored-transformation derivation per templates/SKELETONS-V2.md
